title: Integral Calculus

notes.heading: 1. Substitution, Partial Fractions & Integration by Parts
notes.proseLatex: Standard substitutions collapse logarithmic forms $\int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)| + C$ and quadratic denominators $\int \frac{dx}{x^2+a^2} = \frac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\!\frac{x}{a} + C$. Integration by parts $\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du$ chooses $u$ via ILATE (Inverse-trig, Logarithmic, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential), and unlocks the classic JELET cancellation $\int e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]\,dx = e^x f(x) + C$.

keyFormulas.label: Integration by Parts & e^x [f + f'] Shortcut
keyFormulas.latex: $\int u\,v\,dx = u\int v\,dx - \int\!\left(u'\int v\,dx\right)dx,\qquad \int e^x\bigl[f(x)+f'(x)\bigr]dx = e^x f(x) + C$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Spot self-cancelling e^x(f + f') integrals immediately.

stepsLatex: Identify $f(x) = \frac{1}{(x+1)^2}$ whose derivative is $f'(x) = -\frac{2}{(x+1)^3}$; hence integral $= \frac{e^x}{(x+1)^2} + C$.

notes.heading: 2. Definite Integral Symmetry, King's Rule &Wallis Formula
notes.proseLatex: King's property $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = \int_a^b f(a+b-x)\,dx$ pairs $I$ with its reflection so $2I = \int_a^b [f(x)+f(a+b-x)]\,dx$; when $f(a+b-x)=f(x)$, any ratio $\int_a^b \frac{f(x)}{f(x)+f(a+b-x)}\,dx$ equals $\frac{b-a}{2}$ immediately. On symmetric intervals $[-a,a]$, odd integrands ($f(-x)=-f(x)$) integrate to $0$, while even integrands double over $[0,a]$.

keyFormulas.label: King's Property & Symmetric Interval Rules
keyFormulas.latex: $\int_a^b \frac{f(x)\,dx}{f(x)+f(a+b-x)} = \frac{b-a}{2},\qquad \int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \begin{cases}0,& f\text{ odd}\\ 2\int_0^a f(x)\,dx,& f\text{ even}\end{cases}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Evaluate definite integrals via symmetry without finding antiderivatives.

notes.heading: 3. Leibniz Integral Rule & Bounded Area
notes.proseLatex: Differentiating an integral with variable limits $F(x) = \int_{g(x)}^{h(x)} f(t)\,dt$ gives $F'(x) = f(h(x))h'(x) - f(g(x))g'(x)$ (fundamental tool for integral limits of $0/0$ type!). Geometrically, the geometric area enclosed between $y = f(x)$ and $y = g(x)$ on $[a,b]$ is $\int_a^b |f(x) - g(x)|\,dx$, splitting at every root where the curves cross.

keyFormulas.label: Newton-Leibniz Variable-Limit Derivative & Area
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Differentiate variable-limit integrals and compute positive geometric area.

wbjeebTraps: When asked for 'area bounded by $y = \sin x$ and the $x$-axis on $[0, 2\pi]$', integrate $|\sin x|$ to get $4$, NOT $\int_0^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx = 0$.
In variable-limit differentiation $\frac{d}{dx}\int_0^{x^2} \cos t\,dt$, remember the chain-rule factor $2x$: answer is $2x\cos(x^2)$, NOT $\cos(x^2)$.
Before substituting $t = \tan x$ in a definite integral across $x = \pi/2$, split at the discontinuity $\pi/2$ — blind substitution produces negative answers for positive integrands!

conceptPrimer.heading: Standard Forms: $f'/f$ and the Arctangent Family
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\int\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx = \ln|f(x)| + C$ and $\int\frac{dx}{x^2+a^2} = \frac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{a} + C$ kill whole question classes on sight. Micro-check: $\int\frac{2x}{x^2+1}dx = \ln(x^2+1) + C$ (numerator is half the derivative of the denominator's inside).

conceptPrimer.heading: By Parts, ILATE & the $e^x[f + f']$ Cancellation
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du$ with $u$ chosen by ILATE (Inverse-trig, Log, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential). The JELET favourite: $\int e^x[f(x) + f'(x)]\,dx = e^x f(x) + C$. Micro-check: $\int e^x(\sin x + \cos x)\,dx = e^x\sin x + C$ since $\frac{d}{dx}\sin x = \cos x$.

conceptPrimer.heading: King's Rule & the Ratio Shortcut
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = \int_a^b f(a+b-x)\,dx$; adding the two gives $2I$. When $f(a+b-x) = f(x)$, the ratio $\int_a^b\frac{f(x)}{f(x)+f(a+b-x)}\,dx$ collapses to $\frac{b-a}{2}$. Micro-check: $\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{\sin x}{\sin x + \cos x}dx = \frac{\pi/2}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Odd & Even Integrand Symmetry on $[-a, a]$
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $f(-x) = -f(x)$ (odd) integrates to $0$ over $[-a, a]$; $f(-x) = f(x)$ (even) doubles over $[0, a]$. Micro-check: $\int_{-1}^{1} x^3\,dx = 0$ but $\int_{-1}^{1} x^2\,dx = \frac{2}{3}$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Leibniz Integral Rule (Variable Limits)
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: $F(x) = \int_{g(x)}^{h(x)} f(t)\,dt \Rightarrow F'(x) = f(h(x))h'(x) - f(g(x))g'(x)$ — the chain-rule factors are mandatory, and this is the tool for integral-type $0/0$ limits. Micro-check: $\frac{d}{dx}\int_0^{x^2}\cos t\,dt = 2x\cos(x^2)$, not $\cos(x^2)$.

conceptPrimer.heading: Geometric Area: Absolutize and Split
conceptPrimer.proseLatex: Area between $y = f(x)$ and $y = g(x)$ on $[a, b]$ is $\int_a^b|f - g|\,dx$ — split at every crossing; the plain integral can cancel to zero. Micro-check: area under $\sin x$ on $[0, 2\pi]$: $\int_0^{2\pi}|\sin x|\,dx = 4$, while $\int_0^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx = 0$.

memoryHooks: ILATE: Inverse, Log, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential.
$e^x[f + f'] \to e^x f$ — recognize and skip work.
Odd kills, even doubles on $[-a, a]$.
Leibniz: multiply by the LIMIT's derivative, both ends.
Area questions: absolutize and split at crossings.
$\sin x$ over a full period: net $0$, area $4$.
commonMistakes: Reporting $\int_0^{2\pi}\sin x\,dx = 0$ as the bounded area.
Dropping chain-rule factors in Leibniz differentiation.
Using L'Hospital-style limits on integrals without the Leibniz rule.
Wallis ladder sign errors for odd $n$.
examChecklist: Choose $u$ by ILATE for every by-parts question.
Reflect with King's rule when the interval ratio appears.
Exploit odd/even symmetry before computing anything.
Leibniz: $f(h)h' - f(g)g'$ with both chain factors.
Geometric area: $|f - g|$ with splits at crossings.
Wallis for even/odd powers of $\sin$ on $[0, \pi/2]$.
Split definite integrals at interior discontinuities.
